html:
In November 2017 the Zimbabwean army took control of Harare and placed President Robert Mugabe under house arrest, forcing him to resign on 21 November after 37 years in power.

Mugabe, then 93, had just sacked his vice president Emmerson Mnangagwa, a veteran of the liberation war, apparently to clear the way for his wife Grace. The army, close to Mnangagwa, moved in, while saying it was not a coup. Huge crowds celebrated in Harare, and parliament began impeachment before he resigned.

Mnangagwa became president. Hopes of reform faded as the economy stayed weak and soldiers shot protesters after the 2018 election. The ruling party built in the liberation war kept its hold on Zimbabwe.
sum: In November 2017 the Zimbabwean army took control of Harare and placed President Robert Mugabe under house arrest, forcing him to resign on 21 November after 37 years in power.
